chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Faddal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Mu'awiya, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Hatim, so he said: 'It is what is between the Black Stone and the door.' And I asked him why it was called the Hatim, so he said: 'Because people break each other (i.e., crowd and push one another there).'

key_terms.الْحَطِيمُ: The Hatim, a semi-circular wall structure adjacent to the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What is the Hatim of the Kaaba and why is it called that?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the architectural definition of the Hatim (Hateem) as the semi-circular wall adjacent to the Kaaba, distinguishing it from the main structure. The etymological link to 'breaking' or 'crushing' (tahrim) reflects the physical pressure of pilgrims during Tawaf, a practical detail relevant to the chapter’s discussion on expiations for inadvertent violations of Ihram conditions.
